receiver.message_back:
Counsel,

Thank you for the draft. Buyer has reviewed and is prepared to continue discussions, but the current draft is too limited in both economics and protections for a transaction of this nature.

Buyer’s counterproposal is as follows:

1. Purchase Price. Revise the purchase price to USD 36,000,000. Buyer’s position reflects the limited diligence completed to date and the narrow protection package in the initial draft.

2. Closing Timeline and Conditions. The 30-day outside date is not workable. Please revise to a 60-day outside date and include customary closing conditions, including completion of Buyer’s diligence to Buyer’s reasonable satisfaction, no material adverse effect, required third-party and governmental approvals, bring-down of representations and warranties, covenant compliance, and delivery of customary officer certificates and ancillary documents.

3. Representations. The Seller representation package needs to be expanded materially. At a minimum, please add customary representations regarding organization and authority, due authorization, enforceability, title to the shares, capitalization, subsidiaries, financial statements without Seller-knowledge qualification, absence of undisclosed liabilities, absence of material changes, compliance with law, permits, taxes, material contracts, litigation, employees/benefits, intellectual property, data/privacy, related-party matters, and brokers.

4. Covenants. Please add ordinary-course operating covenants between signing and closing, restrictions on dividends, debt, compensation changes, related-party transactions, capital expenditures outside budget, material contracts, and dispositions, plus access to books, records, management, and advisors.

5. Remedies/Indemnity. The draft should include a customary indemnification framework for breaches of representations, covenants, pre-closing taxes, and fraud, with appropriate survival periods, procedures, and an escrow or holdback to support recovery.

6. Payment Mechanics. Buyer cannot agree to language prohibiting all setoff, deduction, withholding, or counterclaim. Please revise to permit withholding required by law and agreed purchase price adjustments, escrow, indemnity, or other remedies under the agreement.

7. Confidentiality. The confidentiality covenant is generally acceptable as a starting point, but should include standard exceptions for required regulatory disclosures, financing process disclosures, diligence advisors, representatives, and disclosures necessary to enforce the agreement, each subject to customary protections.

Please provide a revised draft reflecting the above. Buyer remains willing to move efficiently, but only with appropriate price, diligence, and contractual protections.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
Counsel for Buyer

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 36,000,000 for the Shares (the "Purchase Price"), payable in immediately available funds at Closing. The Purchase Price shall be paid without setoff, deduction, withholding, or counterclaim, except for (a) any withholding required by applicable law, (b) amounts expressly required to be deposited into the Escrow Fund pursuant to Section 7, and (c) any purchase price adjustment or other deduction expressly agreed in writing by the parties in this Agreement. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize any required withholding and shall provide Seller with reasonable prior notice of any proposed withholding.

2. Closing; Closing Conditions. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable following satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement and in any event no later than 60 days after signing, unless extended by mutual written agreement. Each party's obligation to close is conditioned on: (a) the accuracy of the other party's representations and warranties at signing and at Closing, except for inaccuracies that would not reasonably be expected to be material to the Company or the transactions contemplated hereby; (b) performance in all material respects of the other party's covenants required to be performed before Closing; (c) receipt of required governmental approvals and material third-party consents identified on the disclosure schedules; (d) absence of any law, order, or injunction prohibiting Closing; and (e) delivery of customary officer certificates and ancillary documents. Buyer's obligation to close is further conditioned on: (i) no Material Adverse Effect having occurred after signing; and (ii) Buyer's completion of confirmatory diligence to its reasonable satisfaction within 20 days after signing; provided that Buyer may not rely on this diligence condition with respect to any matter fairly disclosed in the disclosure schedules or in written diligence materials made available to Buyer prior to signing. For purposes of this Agreement, "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, or effect that is materially adverse to the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, taken as a whole, excluding effects arising from general economic, industry, market, legal, geopolitical, or public health conditions, changes in law or accounting standards, announcement or pendency of the transaction, or actions taken at Buyer's request, except to the extent such effects disproportionately affect the Company relative to similarly situated businesses.

3. Representations and Warranties of Seller. Seller represents and warrants to Buyer that, except as set forth in the disclosure schedules: (a) Seller and the Company are duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under their respective jurisdictions of organization and have requisite power and authority to own their assets and conduct their businesses; (b) Seller has full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement, and this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered by Seller and constitutes a valid and binding obligation of Seller, enforceable against Seller in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy, insolvency, fraudulent transfer, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws and equitable principles; (c) Seller owns the Shares free and clear of all liens other than transfer restrictions under applicable securities laws, and upon Closing Buyer will acquire good and valid title to the Shares; (d) the capitalization of the Company is as set forth on the disclosure schedules, and there are no outstanding options, warrants, convertible securities, or other rights to acquire equity securities of the Company except as disclosed; (e) the Company's subsidiaries, if any, are identified on the disclosure schedules; (f) the financial statements delivered to Buyer fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated therein, subject to normal year-end adjustments and the notes thereto; (g) the Company has no undisclosed liabilities required to be reflected on a balance sheet prepared in accordance with the accounting principles used in preparing the financial statements, other than liabilities incurred in the ordinary course since the most recent balance sheet date; (h) since the most recent balance sheet date, there has been no Material Adverse Effect and the Company has operated in the ordinary course in all material respects; (i) the Company is, and during the applicable limitations period has been, in material compliance with applicable laws and holds all material permits required for its business; (j) the Company has timely filed all material tax returns required to be filed and has paid all material taxes due and payable, except those being contested in good faith and adequately reserved; (k) the material contracts of the Company are listed on the disclosure schedules, are in full force and effect, and neither the Company nor, to Seller's knowledge, any counterparty is in material breach thereof; (l) there is no material litigation, arbitration, governmental investigation, or proceeding pending or, to Seller's knowledge, threatened against the Company; (m) the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment, labor, and employee benefit laws, and all material benefit plans are identified on the disclosure schedules; (n) the Company owns or has valid rights to use the intellectual property used in its business and, to Seller's knowledge, the conduct of the business does not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights in any material respect; (o) the Company is in material compliance with applicable data privacy and security laws and has not experienced any material unauthorized access to personal information requiring notice under applicable law; (p) except as disclosed, there are no material related-party transactions between the Company, on the one hand, and Seller or its affiliates, on the other hand; and (q) no broker, finder, or investment banker is entitled to any fee or commission from Buyer or the Company in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement based on arrangements made by Seller.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement, all negotiations relating hereto, and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby are confidential and shall not be disclosed by either party except to its and its affiliates' directors, officers, employees, professional advisors, financing sources, prospective financing sources, insurers, auditors, and other representatives who have a need to know and are informed of the confidential nature of the information; as required by applicable law, regulation, stock exchange rule, subpoena, court order, or governmental authority; in connection with the financing process, confirmatory diligence, or enforcement of this Agreement; or with the prior written consent of the other party. The disclosing party shall, to the extent legally permissible and reasonably practicable, provide prior notice of any legally required disclosure and reasonably cooperate to limit the scope of such disclosure. Each party shall be responsible for breaches of this Section by its representatives.

5. Interim Operating Covenants. From signing until Closing or earlier termination, Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course of business in all material respects and use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve its business, assets, employees, customer and supplier relationships, and permits. Without Buyer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, Seller shall not cause or permit the Company to: (a) declare or pay dividends or distributions outside the ordinary course; (b) incur material indebtedness other than ordinary-course trade payables or borrowings under existing facilities; (c) materially increase compensation or benefits except as required by law, existing agreements, or ordinary-course practice; (d) enter into or amend material related-party transactions; (e) make capital expenditures materially outside the approved budget; (f) enter into, amend, terminate, or waive material rights under material contracts outside the ordinary course; (g) sell, lease, license, or dispose of material assets outside the ordinary course; (h) issue, redeem, or otherwise change equity securities; (i) settle material litigation outside the ordinary course; or (j) make or change material tax elections outside the ordinary course. Seller shall provide Buyer and its representatives reasonable access, during normal business hours and upon reasonable notice, to the Company's books, records, management, advisors, and facilities for confirmatory diligence, subject to confidentiality obligations, privilege protections, applicable law, and reasonable measures to avoid undue disruption.

6. Termination. This Agreement may be terminated before Closing by mutual written agreement; by either party if Closing has not occurred by the 60-day outside date, provided the terminating party is not then in material breach; by either party if a final non-appealable order permanently prohibits Closing; by Buyer during the 20-day confirmatory diligence period if Buyer reasonably determines in good faith that diligence has identified a material adverse matter not fairly disclosed prior to signing; or by the non-breaching party for an uncured material breach by the other party after 10 business days' written notice, if such breach would cause a closing condition not to be satisfied.

7. Indemnification; Escrow; Remedies. From and after Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer and the Company for losses arising from: (a) breaches of Seller's representations and warranties; (b) breaches of Seller's covenants; (c) pre-Closing taxes of the Company to the extent not otherwise reflected in the final Purchase Price or disclosed reserves; and (d) fraud. Non-fundamental representations shall survive for 12 months after Closing; fundamental representations regarding organization, authority, title to Shares, capitalization, taxes, and brokers shall survive for 36 months after Closing, except that tax matters shall survive until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations; covenants shall survive according to their terms; and fraud claims shall survive as provided by law. Seller shall have no liability for breaches of non-fundamental representations unless aggregate losses exceed USD 360,000, after which Seller shall be liable only for amounts in excess of such threshold. Seller's aggregate liability for breaches of non-fundamental representations shall not exceed USD 3,600,000. These basket and cap limitations shall not apply to breaches of fundamental representations, covenants, pre-Closing taxes, or fraud; provided that Seller's aggregate liability shall not exceed the Purchase Price except in the case of fraud. At Closing, USD 1,800,000 of the Purchase Price shall be deposited with a mutually acceptable escrow agent for 12 months to secure Seller's indemnification obligations for non-fundamental representation claims, with any remaining amount released to Seller promptly thereafter, subject to pending claims. Indemnification claims shall be made by written notice describing the claim in reasonable detail, and third-party claims shall be subject to customary defense, cooperation, and settlement procedures. Except for claims for fraud, equitable relief, and disputes regarding the escrow, the indemnification rights in this Section constitute Buyer's sole and exclusive monetary remedy after Closing for matters arising under this Agreement.
